work.text: When the plants and trees are introduced in larger compositions their linear quality is often still more accentuated, [which] sometimes produces effects not unlike those of silk embroideries or woven textiles.

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

work.text: He utilized plump, profound brushwork and precise color, creating a unique style.

moment.text: He returned to his home in 1643 and when Nanking fell to the Manchus (1645) he entered the Buddhist priesthood, fleeing to the mountains in 1646, possibly in consequence of some anti-Manchu activities.

source.author: Fang Chao-ying
source.title: Ch‘ên Hung-shou
source.publisher: in Arthur W. Hummel (ed.), Eminent Chinese of the Ch‘ing Period, vol. I, US Government Printing Office (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: Six years later he returned to his home where [he] died.
matters.lead: After the years in the mountains:

source.author: Fang Chao-ying
source.title: Ch‘ên Hung-shou
source.publisher: in Arthur W. Hummel (ed.), Eminent Chinese of the Ch‘ing Period, vol. I, US Government Printing Office (Internet Archive scan)

matters.text: Painted two years before his death, after the upheavals of the conquest, this fan shows an untroubled retreat: figures in a thatched pavilion shaded by pines and banana plants.
